newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mixed, business slow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mixed, business slow.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were mixed on Wednesday, supported by tight nearby supplies but weighed down by lackluster demand, dealers said.
"It has been quiet for quite some time," a St Louis dealer said. "We seem to be susceptible to whatever the (CBOT) grain markets are doing."

"We still have a little bit of limited run time at the flour mills in Buffalo," a Buffalo dealer said. "But business does not seem to change much. There is no feature in feed demand, but it should improve later in March."

One Carolinas dealer said supplies were tight. "Most of the interest is from merchandisers trying to cover sales they have made. Flour mills are not running well, so they just call around everywhere trying to fill their orders. That has held the market up."

He noted that demand was featureless. "As far as retail business, there is just zero feed demand. So what feed is being made is pretty much going to people who have integrated business, like turkeys, broilers and hogs."
Dealers also said with the transition of winter into springtime, business was slowing down as an increasing number of High Plains cattle switch to feeding on grass.
